title: a getter in an argument whose body throws an ordinary Error still needs a contract, and the two backends refuse it with different diagnostic sets

xfail.reason: the fork reports only [SMITHERS1303@8:19] where the reference reports [SMITHERS1105@8:19, SMITHERS1303@8:19]. The cause is not a missed shape: THE GO BACKEND IMPLEMENTS NO SMITHERS1105 AND NO SMITHERS1106 AT ALL. Re-checked 2026-08-28: neither code is ever REPORTED by the fork — `grep '"SMITHERS1105"|"SMITHERS1106"' compiler/forkbridge/` finds no report site, and SMITHERS1106 appears in the fork nowhere at all. (The earlier wording, "neither code appears anywhere in the fork", is no longer literally true and should not be used to check the claim: `SMITHERS1105` now appears in three fork COMMENTS — `compiler/forkbridge/mustconsume.go.txt` and two places in `compiler/forkbridge/lowering.go.txt` — that describe the reference's behaviour without implementing it. Grep for the quoted report argument, not the bare code.) So on every fallible accessor, constructor and generator the two backends have always disagreed about how loudly to refuse — and the disagreement was invisible, because no corpus case reached either code and a prior code-set subtraction counted them as covered. It became visible only when the panic non-widening rule removed SMITHERS1101 from the panicking half of the same class, leaving the ordinary-Error half as the residual. BOTH BACKENDS REFUSE THIS PROGRAM, so this is not a fail-open and no checked failure escapes: SMITHERS1303 is the refusal that matters here, because it is the one about a failure channel crossing a value edge, and both backends report it at the same authored position. They disagree only about the additional accessor-shape refusal. WHICH IS RIGHT: the specification does not name either code. It requires only that the program be refused — failures.mdx:190 makes a Result must-use and the callback value edge carries a checked failure out of the getter — and both backends satisfy that. SMITHERS1105 ('constructors and accessors cannot carry a Result channel in this POC') is a declared POC lowering boundary of the same family as SMITHERS1503, not a normative sentence, so the reference's extra diagnostic is a stricter implementation of an unspecified detail rather than a rule the fork is missing. NEITHER BACKEND SHOULD BE CHANGED ON THE STRENGTH OF THIS MARKER. Retire it in one of two ways, both deliberate: if the accessor limitation is kept and made normative, the fork implements SMITHERS1105 and SMITHERS1106 and this marker is deleted unchanged; if accessors are allowed to carry a channel, or the limitation is declared implementation-defined, the DECLARATION here drops to [SMITHERS1303@8:19] and the marker goes with it. The panicking twin of this program is now ACCEPTED on both backends and executes — a getter that panics has no failure channel to lose, which is exactly why it lost its refusal and this one did not.
xfail.doc: specification/failures.mdx:190 — 'A Result MUST be treated as a must-use value. A source program MUST NOT silently discard a Result without returning, matching, transforming, inspecting, or unwrapping it.' The page names no diagnostic code for an accessor that cannot carry a channel; SMITHERS1105 and SMITHERS1106 are declared POC boundaries (poc/src/language/semantic.ts), which is why this marker records the asymmetry rather than picking a side.

notes: Written as a deliberate pair with 09-foreign-calls/an-accessor-may-read-its-state-through-a-panicking-helper and 09-foreign-calls/a-constructor-a-getter-and-a-setter-may-all-abort, and neither half means much alone. The panicking accessor is now accepted and runs; this one, byte-comparable but throwing an ORDINARY recoverable Error, is still refused on both backends. That contrast is the substance: the non-widening rule removed a refusal from exactly the shape that had no failure channel to lose, and removed none from the shape that does. Before this case, SMITHERS1105 and SMITHERS1106 were two of the codes the reference implements, the fork does not, and no corpus case probed — the worst of the three categories in conformance/COVERAGE.md's code-set subtraction, because it produces no divergence in either direction ever. It is pinned now at the cost of one marker.
